newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto Q1 operating income rises.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto Q1 operating income rises.

text.p: Monsanto Co said Tuesday its first quarter operating earnings, excluding a writeoff and an accounting change charge, amounted to $343 million or $0.56 a share.

Earlier, it reported record net income of $274 million or $0.45 a share, after a $0.10 a share writeoff of acquired in-process research and development, as well as a $0.01 a share accounting change charge. That compared with year-ago first quarter net income of $260 millon or $0.43 a share.
Monsanto said the acquired in-process research writeoff was related to its acquisition of Asgrow Agronomics and a smaller seed company in Brazil.

As previously announced, Monsanto has agreements to acquire Holden's Foundation Seeds Inc, Corn States Hybrid Service Inc and Corn States International. It also has a definitive agreement to acquire the remaining shares of Calgene Inc that it does not already own.
"We're continuing to get strong performance from our business operations, allowing us to make substantial investments in growth," Monsanto Chairman Robert Shapiro said.

"At the same time, we're positioning our life science and chemical businesses to get off to a strong start once the spinoff is complete," he added in a statement. Monsanto has previously said it will spin off chemical operations.

Monsanto said its agricultural products division had first quarter sales of $1.07 billion, up from $825.0 million a year ago, and operating income of $224 million after the research charge, down from $272.0 million a year ago. Excluding the charge, the agricultural operating profit would have been a record, Monsanto said.

G.D. Searle pharmaceutical sales in the quarter rose to $515 million from $477 million, but operating income fell to $55 million from $60 million. The year-ago quarter benefited from cost-sharing alliances, Monsanto said.
Food ingredient sales were down to $260 million from $266 million, but operating profit rose to $43 million from $25 million due to reduced costs.

Chemicals sales were $732 million, compared with $736 million a year ago, while operating profit rose to $81 million from $64 million. Monsanto said earnings rose for its Saflex plastic interlayer and performance materials and increased moderately for fibers and specialty products.
